title: fix(spec): stop teaching the retired ETL layer as a live retry surface (#6630, part 1)
body:
Part of objectstack-ai/objectstack#6630 (part 1 of 2 — see the [claim-amendment comment](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/6630#issuecomment-5226105668)). **No `Fixes` line on purpose:** the issue stays open for part 2, which handles `automation/flow.zod.ts`'s three sites once #5593 releases that file.

## What was wrong

#6414 retired the whole L2 ETL layer — `automation/etl.zod.ts` and its 9 defs / 27 exported names, with the export absence pinned in `automation/sync-retirement.test.ts`. `shared/retry-policy.zod.ts` knew: exactly one stanza (the module TSDoc's `automation/etl.zod.ts` bullet) was moved to the past tense. Every other mention in the file stayed in the present, and one of them is not a comment.

The load-bearing one is the `retryDelayMs` tombstone. `shared/retired-key.ts` describes that string as the upgrade channel in its own words — *"an agent bumping `@objectstack/spec` sees THIS string, not our docs site"* — and it enumerated **four** surfaces on which the converged spelling applies:

> … `job.retryPolicy`, a `try_catch` node's `retry`, `flow.errorHandling` **and an ETL pipeline's `retry`**.

The fourth had been deleted in the same major. So the one message guaranteed to reach an author or agent migrating `retryDelayMs` to `backoffMs` was recommending a surface on which `tsc` now reports TS2724/TS2305 — the prescription spending its credibility to send the reader to a compile error.

## What changed

Text only. Nothing alters what any schema accepts: `retryPolicyShape()` and `RetryPolicySchema` keep their exact key sets, bounds and defaults, and `retryDelayMs` is still rejected, still with a prescription. `check:authorable-surface` is green with no baseline edit.

**`packages/spec/src/shared/retry-policy.zod.ts`** — the five sites the issue numbers 1-5:

| Site | Was | Now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| tombstone string (`retiredKey`) | four surfaces, incl. "an ETL pipeline's `retry`" | the three that still carry the policy; prescription untouched |
| `RetryPolicySchema` TSDoc | "`Flow.errorHandling` **and `ETLPipeline.retry`** carry the same contract" | `Flow.errorHandling` carries it; ETL "did the same until #6414 retired the L2 ETL layer" |
| `retryPolicyShape` TSDoc | "**Two of the four** surfaces … cannot simply reference" | "**One of the three** …", with the retired second named parenthetically |
| module TSDoc, the `maxAttempts`-tombstone paragraph | "The `maxAttempts` tombstone on that block **is the whole migration channel**" | there is no such tombstone — see below |
| module TSDoc arithmetic | "the **four** surfaces share one declaration"; "the **two** of them that are `.strict()`" | three / one |

The `maxAttempts` paragraph was the subtler harm: it told a future maintainer auditing "is the #4962 convergence fully migrated?" that a channel exists. It does not, and the authority says so directly — `migrations/registry.ts`'s D3 `etl-pipeline-layer-retired` entry: *"The `maxAttempts` `retiredKey()` tombstone goes with the shape that carried it, which is strictly stronger than the tombstone: there is no longer a `retry` block to author the key into. Route 3 — no carrier key, no parse site, so no D2 conversion and no tombstone; `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` plus this entry are the declaration."* The paragraph now states that, and names the real door (`tsc`, TS2724/TS2305).

**`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`** — the `retry-policy-converged` doc stanza: the heading's count, the two present-tense clauses, and the same false "its `maxAttempts` tombstone carries the rename AND the default change" claim, now replaced with the absorption fact (#4962's `etl-retry-converged-onto-retry-policy` was ABSORBED into `etl-pipeline-layer-retired` inside the same unreleased major).

**Two adjacent counts the audit's `ETL` grep could not see**, both invalidated by the same retirement and both one word: `retry-policy.zod.ts`'s tombstone comment ("two of the **four** owning shapes are not `.strict()`" / "on the **two** strict surfaces") and `conversions/registry.ts:3715` (the same "four owning shapes"). Flagging them explicitly because they sit outside the issue's numbered inventory; leaving them would have shipped a half-corrected count two lines above a corrected one.

**Out of scope, untouched:** `automation/flow.zod.ts` sites 6a-c. That file is inside #5593's in-flight surface; part 2 takes them, including "the other three" → "the other two".

## The new pin

No pre-existing assertion could see this drift. Every one of them matched the *prescription* — `/backoffMs/` in `shared/retry-policy.test.ts` and `system/job.test.ts`, `/retryDelayMs/` in `automation/control-flow.test.ts`, `flow.errorHandling` in `automation/flow.test.ts` — and never the enumeration. `shared/retry-policy.test.ts` gains one that asserts the substance in both directions: every live surface named, no retired surface named, prescription intact.

There is deliberately no ADR-0112 `code`/`status` assertion here, and the test says why: `retiredKey()` is a Zod `never` whose issue carries the guidance as its `message`, so for this rejection class the wording IS the whole contract (#5240) and there is no envelope to assert.

**Reverse verification, direction predicted before running: plain red.** Restoring the deleted enumeration item turned exactly one test red, on exactly the intended assertion, with the other 8 844 green — which is itself the measurement that nothing before could see this:

```
 ❯ src/shared/retry-policy.test.ts (13 tests | 1 failed)
     × the tombstone enumerates exactly the surfaces that still carry the policy (#6630)

AssertionError: the prescription must not point at a surface #6414 retired:
  expected '`retryDelayMs` was removed in @object…' not to match /\bETL\b/i
 Test Files  1 failed | 344 passed (345)
      Tests  1 failed | 8844 passed (8845)
```

## Generated artifacts

Two reference pages regenerated and committed unedited — the tombstone's `.describe()` reaches them, which `check:docs` caught:

- `content/docs/references/automation/control-flow.mdx`
- `content/docs/references/system/job.mdx`

One line each, the `retryDelayMs [REMOVED]` row. The `{@link}`-bearing TSDoc sentences produced no regen; only the `.describe()` did. `content/docs/releases/` untouched.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **345 files / 8845 tests passed**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — green (`tsc --noEmit`, `check:scripts-typecheck`, `check:test-typecheck`; ledger unchanged)
- Every gate in the **TypeScript Type Check** job's generated-artifact set, one by one: `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs`, `check:skill-refs`, `check:skill-docs` — all green after the regen
- Every gate in the **ESLint** job, enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` and run one by one — 31/31 pass, including `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:release-notes`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`
- `eslint` on the three changed source files — clean

Changeset: `@objectstack/spec: patch` — the tombstone guidance is author-visible, so it is a release-noted change rather than a docs-only one.
